story_type: Army heavy-lift helicopters land on a Navy aircraft carrier at sea, deck landing qualification
hook: The Army landed its biggest helicopter on a Navy carrier.
narration: The Army flew its biggest helicopter onto a Navy aircraft carrier, in the middle of the sea.
Soldiers from the 2nd Combat Aviation Brigade took CH-47F Chinooks out east of the Korean peninsula in September 2022.
Their landing pad was USS Ronald Reagan, the Navy's only forward deployed carrier.
From the door, the deck looks tiny, and it never stops moving.
A Chinook has two rotors turning in opposite directions, so it needs no tail rotor to keep from spinning.
On deck, a sailor signaled each pilot down to the landing spot.
Deck landings like these certify Army pilots and aircrews to land on a ship.
outcome: The Army crews set their Chinooks down on the Reagan's flight deck.

location_card.place: USS Ronald Reagan, east of the Korean peninsula

title: Army Chinooks land on a Navy carrier
description:
Soldiers from B Company, 3-2 General Support Aviation Battalion, 2nd Combat Aviation Brigade landed CH-47F Chinook helicopters on USS Ronald Reagan in the waters east of the Korean peninsula on Sept. 26, 2022, during deck landing qualifications.
